problem: The chapter says an offset is booked as two numbers, chainage and length. That is true only for perpendicular offsets. For an oblique offset the angle it makes with the chain line is also needed, otherwise the offset cannot be plotted.
fix: Add: for an oblique offset, also record the angle it makes with the chain line (or the two tie measurements to fixed points), because the chainage and length alone do not fix the point on the plan.

problem: The vertical line in the field book is the chain line itself, not a divider with all chainages on one side and all offsets on the other. As written, a student will book every offset on the right and lose which side of the line the object lies on.
fix: Draw the chain line down the page as the vertical line, write the chainage against it at the point where the offset leaves, and write the offset on the left or the right of the line according to the side of the line on which the object lies.

problem: The bullet says to use the measured length 'in the temperature and sag formulas'. In the sag formula the length that enters the cube is the unsupported span l, not the measured length; only the temperature formula uses the measured length M.
fix: Use the measured length M in the temperature, tension and standardization formulas, and the unsupported span l in the sag formula (multiply by the number of spans to get the total).

problem: EDM and GNSS are used without being expanded, and a reader meeting them for the first time on a phone will not know what they are.
fix: Write 'total station or EDM (electromagnetic distance measurement)' and 'GNSS (global navigation satellite system) antenna' at first use.
